title: UPSTYLE_Backdoor_Investigation_d41
description: Your organization has detected suspicious activity on one of its Linux servers. Initial analysis suggests the presence of a backdoor named UPSTYLE. Your task is to investigate, analyze, and respond to this cybersecurity incident.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of systemd and service management
outcomes: Usage of systemctl for service management
Investigation of systemd service unit files
Identify and locate service names and file paths associated with suspicious activity.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: Your organization has detected suspicious activity on one of its Linux servers. Initial analysis suggests the presence of a backdoor named UPSTYLE. Your task is to investigate, analyze, and respond to this cybersecurity incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host via SSH using the provided credentials. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.
levels.local_content: Access the target host via SSH using the provided credentials. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the network, you noticed unusual outbound connections from the target host. Investigate the running services on the target host to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services.
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, you can use the `systemctl list-units --type=service` command. Look for any services that seem out of place or unfamiliar. The suspicious service running on the target host is named `update.py.service`. The type of the flag is a service name.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the list of running services and look for any that seem out of place or unfamiliar.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Now that you have identified the suspicious service, determine how it is automatically started after a system reboot. This will help you understand the persistence mechanism used by the attacker.
levels.solution: To determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after a system reboot, you can investigate the systemd configuration files. The service is set to start automatically using a systemd service unit file. The type of the flag is a file path.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate the systemd configuration files to find how the service is set to start automatically.

levels.title: Suspicious File Discovery
levels.content: Locate the executable or file associated with the suspicious service. This will help you gather more information about the backdoor and its behavior.
levels.solution: To locate the executable or file associated with the suspicious service, you can check the service unit file to find the path to the executable. The path to the executable associated with the suspicious service is `/usr/local/bin/lab-checkin.sh`. The type of the flag is a file path.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the service unit file to find the path to the executable.
